newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Banks, holdings drive Brussels bourse to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Banks, holdings drive Brussels bourse to new highs.

text.p: Heavy buying of banks and holding companies drove the Brussels bourse to new highs on Monday but dealers said the volume could fade on Tuesday, the last day of the present account.
The Bel-20 index of 20 blue chips ended up 0.50 percent at a new closing high of 2,279.04 points. Earlier the index set a new life high at 2,280.46 points.

Financial issues were the main focus after Friday's announcement of a major reshuffle among holding companies Gevaert, Almanij and Cobepa and a merger between Belgium's seventh and eighth largest banks, Bacob and Paribas Belgium.
Gevaert, whose assets are to be shared out between Almanij and Cobepa in a complex series of transactions, was the star performer on the forward market, adding 12.27 percent to 3,340 francs.

Under the shareout plan, holders of Gevaert shares will receive one "new" Gevaert share and a share in Cobepa. The new Gevaert share is in fact a proxy Almanij share: it can be converted immediately or in three years time.
Cobepa unit Ibel, which will receive some of Gevaert's assets, rose 13.39 percent to 6,010 francs. Ibel will pay a 270 franc extraordinary dividend as part of the plan.
Among blue chips, banks BBL and Kredietbank continued to post strong gains on the expectation they would enter into separate alliances.

"The Bacob/Paribas deal has only increased speculation," one trader said. "Most people are expecting something between Kredietbank and Cera bank and there's speculation (BBL shareholder) Royale Belge will be sold."
KB said on Thursday it was in talks with Dutch Rabobank.
Investors are looking for Royale Belge's main shareholder, AXA-UAP, to give a hint about its future at its annual shareholders meeting on Wednesday.
Generale Bank, Belgium's biggest bank, also rose 150 francs to 14,225 francs.

However, bank Dexia CC bucked the trend, pulled down by shares in its French partner bank Credit Local de France. Paris stocks mostly fell following the surprise showing by the Left in the first round of parliamentary elections held on Sunday.

The French poll was also blamed for the lacklustre performance of holding company Synergia on its first day on Brussels Euro.NM market. A trader at co-lead managers Nedee & Co said the issue was hit by French selling.
